reasons: R04, F21, F03: very high sales growth (>40%) combined with a capital raise and no auditor ICFR attestation (smaller filer) creates pressure and opportunity to present strong results with limited external control testing.
F08, F09: major over-time revenue recognition with significant contract assets/unbilled amounts relies on management estimates of progress, a common area for revenue manipulation.
F10: channel return rights or bill-and-hold arrangements add revenue cut-off and return-reserve judgement risk.
F11: material related-party transactions raise the possibility of non-arm's-length or circular revenue.
F07: an immaterial revision of prior periods shows some prior accounting errors, though judged immaterial.
F12: a single customer at 10-25% of revenue is a moderate concentration risk.
R07, R05: rising leverage and slowing depreciation are mild warning signs (depreciation slowing can inflate earnings).
R08, R19, R18, R01: negative accruals, operating cash flow at or above net income, receivables growing slower than sales and normal DSO argue against aggressive revenue or earnings inflation.
R09, R17, R03, R06, R02: Beneish M-score and Dechow F-score below thresholds, normal asset quality and SG&A, stable margins reduce overall concern.

F01, F04, F05, F14, F15, F16, F17, F18, F19, F24: no material weakness, going concern doubt, auditor change, management turnover, investigations, litigation, covenant issues or critical audit matters.
